OrganizationPeopleResponse.description: Active same-tenant humans only; requires current authentication and flight:read. Private, no-store. Complete serialized response is at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes. AuthorityPrincipalResponse.description: Current complete authority of one same-tenant principal, including inactive targets. Requires authority:write. Private, no-store. required.description: A required input with no observation makes the evaluation insufficient without running the check.

select.description: latest: the observations sharing the newest span start. all: every observation up to the page limit, newest first. latestAtOrBefore: the observations sharing the newest span start at or before an instant another read records. within: every observation whose span start lies in a window another read records, from its start to its end, up to the page limit, newest first.

latestAtOrBefore.description: An earlier read, or the subject-state read, and the field of its latest observation that holds the instant. Without one valid instant the read is empty.

within.description: An earlier read, or the subject-state read, and the fields of its latest observation that hold the start and end of the window. Without one valid start the read is empty; without an end it reads up to the evaluation time.

where.description: Only observations meeting every condition are read, before required, select, applicability and the page limit apply.

items.description: oneOf: the field equals one of the values, or, when it holds a list, the list holds one of them. filled: the field holds a value; absent, null and blank text are not filled, false is.

plans.description: The read reads plans: records about a time that has not come (their span starts after the evaluation instant) are read as soon as they are recorded. Absent: a record is read once its span has started.

onFile.description: What a person calls the record this required read takes, such as "remote pilot certificate". When every required read that is empty names one, the result is insufficient with reason record_not_on_file and says "No … on file."

params.description: Fixed parameters for the check kind. Adoption parameters are added under their own names.

items.description: A value the adopting organization must supply, passed to the check under this name.

The rule applies only when the field of the latest observation of this input equals one of the values. The engine evaluates it; the check never sees an inapplicable subject. When the input is a required read that names the record it takes (onFile) and none is on file, the result says that record is not on file.

whenAbsent.description: When no observation of the input is on record: the rule does not apply, is insufficient, or applies (for a rule that reads either a source’s report or the operator’s own record).

notMetSummary.description: The summary recorded when the field holds none of the values, in place of the engine’s own sentence naming the field.

subjectState.description: Reads what Ledger holds about the evaluated subject itself, such as a flight’s status and declared times. It reaches the check as one observation under this name, and its revision is part of the input digest.

required.description: A required state that Ledger does not hold makes the evaluation insufficient.

wording.description: The rule’s own summary for a result the check returns, keyed by outcome. Placeholders such as {dueAt} are filled only from the check result’s details; when one is not returned the check’s own summary is used. Wording never changes the result.

related.description: Subjects the evaluated subject’s records name. At most one fans out: the rule then gives one result per related subject.

items.description: A subject the evaluated subject’s records name, which reads may be about.

field.description: subject or secondarySubject: that role of each observation, as currently resolved. Any other path: a reference field ({ id, scope }) in each observation, resolved through alias resolutions inside the evidence cut.

fanOut.description: true: one result per distinct related subject. false: the read must name exactly one; two or more is conflicting.

whenNone.description: The result for the evaluated subject when the read names no related subject. empty (not with fanOut): the reads about it are empty and the check runs, for reads that only add to what the evaluated subject’s own records show.

whenNoneSummary.description: The summary recorded when the read names no related subject, in place of the engine’s own sentence naming the read, such as "No dock or ground station is named on the flight plan."

requeue.description: Which evaluated subjects are still worth evaluating again when a record about this related subject changes: those whose window has not ended, or ended within endedWithinDays. A subject with no recorded end is queued. A skipped subject keeps its last evaluation; the queueing work for the event records how many it skipped. Absent: every subject that names it is queued.

windowEnd.description: A read about the evaluated subject, or the subject-state read, and the field of its latest observation that holds when the evaluated subject’s window ends.

endedWithinDays.description: Also re-queue a subject whose window ended at most this many days ago. Absent: 0.

relieves.description: Rules of other packs this provision relieves. Only a rule whose source is a waiver or exemption may declare it. While an adoption of this pack in active mode is in effect, an evaluation of a relieved rule is recorded as relieved; in shadow, as what it would relieve.

items.description: The pack and the ids of its checked rules this provision relieves. The registry refuses a relief of the rule’s own pack, of an unregistered pack or of a rule id no registered version of that pack holds.

population.description: Who the rule is meant for: each member is evaluated when the pack is adopted, revised or succeeded, and when it joins, whether or not a record the rule reads exists about it. Absent: the rule is evaluated for the subjects whose records it reads.

anyOf.description: Every subject of the target kind the organization has on record: a Ledger subject of the kind, or a subject a current observation names as its subject, secondary subject or in a reference field.

The subjects of the target kind that current observations of this type, meeting the conditions, name at the field: for example the people role records name as remote pilots, or the aircraft a fleet record lists.

section.description: The id of the section of the pack version the rule belongs to, one its sections list declares.

paragraph.description: The paragraph the rule reads, as a reader cites it, such as “§ 108.40(a)(3)(i)” or “Provision 3”.

MissionDepartureAuthorizationCommand.description: Final authorization after the caller retains a live exclusive allocation and establishes full remaining operation fit. On first issuance, atomically validate the exact release and current authority, including expectedPrincipalRevision, and grant one nonrenewable lease per tenant/Ledger flight. Retain fixed attempt/allocation bindings; tenant/allocation identity binds one flight and attempt. Exact original-key retries recover the same unexpired lease without a new safety-context or principal-revision comparison; current authentication and scope checks remain. Later accepted safety changes do not revoke the issued lease. Expired restart replay fails; no key, attempt or allocation can obtain another authorization for this flight. Atomically retain a fresh fit witness and once-per-flight consumption with the physical transition across restart. An unused expired lease leaves the flight held or abandoned; replacement requires a later explicit protocol or new Ledger flight. No continuous post-takeoff validity or control claim beyond the mission interval is implied.

schema.description: A read-only mission comparison. Every risk-accepted area control version overlapping the mission interval is considered, at most 512; each is evaluated by the applicability rule its pinned type declares. Those that apply are candidates, at most 64, compared with the route; the rest are listed under notApplicable with their applicability records. This is not flight release, implementation, enforcement, risk reduction or evaluator activation.

items.description: One exact risk-accepted area control version overlapping the planned mission interval: a control record whose type describes an area, accepted on a safety-record hazard of any origin. controlEventId is its version event, controlDigest its body digest, template its pinned control type, and an open-ended interval ends with the planned mission interval. Proposals alone are not candidates. It applies to the flight: its applicability record says why, for the exact mission revision.

One considered accepted area control version that does not apply to the exact mission revision, by the applicability rule its pinned type declares, with its title and the area its type describes, so a reader needs no other read to list or place it. The applicability record holds what was measured, what the control declares and the rule by digest. It is not a candidate: route review does not compare it, the release does not need it outside and no briefing lists it.

get.description: Returns the state of one mission release now: scheduled, current, expired, changed or pending, with the current context digest. Needs `flight:read`.

schema.description: As-of information only; GET must never trigger departure. Precedence: expired at window end; changed for known mission, aircraft, policy or safety-context mismatch; pending when matching validity cannot be established; then scheduled before window start or current within it. Higher accepted mission/control changes block new authorizations before projection, including a higher failed mission. Matching failed or unsupported evidence cannot establish current validity. nextBoundary is a recheck time, not a guaranteed validity lease. A separately issued finite departure lease retains its original authorization point.

get.summary: Read one briefing of a flight
get.description: Returns one briefing recorded for a flight, with the people it was given to. Needs `flight:read`.

briefing.description: Immutable exact briefing content and named recipient population, limited to 1 MiB of serialized JSON. Mission, aircraft, safety context and unchanged release policy derive from the cited release; each selected control and acceptance must match one retained candidate. Digest of the complete record identifies what recipients attest to reviewing. No delivery, operational-crew coverage, control implementation or release/departure prerequisite is established. It lists one or more exact controls, each once and in the order of the release's candidates, with the content of each at the same position; one acknowledgement acknowledges all of them. It pins the controls in scope the author saw, by digest, whenever the command named that digest.

population.description: Server-resolved recipients sorted uniquely by principalId. Digest commits this complete object excluding digest. Retained principalRevision is historical identity, not an acknowledgement authority revision. Membership and its denominator never change with later deactivation, grants or crew assignments.

items.description: One exact risk-accepted area control version overlapping the planned mission interval: a control record whose type describes an area, accepted on a safety-record hazard of any origin. controlEventId is its version event, controlDigest its body digest, template its pinned control type, and an open-ended interval ends with the planned mission interval. Proposals alone are not candidates.

center.description: Operator-authored WGS84 circle center in degrees.

controls.description: The controls in scope for a flight as a person saw them: each control version, its wording and its result at that moment, with the mission revision route review read. digest is canonicalDigest of {version, controls, notApplicable, complete, mission}. A briefing or departure record that carries it pins this list; it is never a verdict and blocks nothing.

items.description: One accepted control version in scope for the flight, in its own words: in force now, or accepted to take effect later, or with an interval that has ended.

period.description: Where the read falls in the control’s effective interval. upcoming: it takes effect at effectiveFrom and is not evaluated before then. ended: its interval ended at effectiveUntil and it is no longer evaluated. Only a current control has results from its check.

check.description: rule: the organization’s rule from this accepted control, run by the evaluator. route_review: route review keeps the planned route clear of its area. person: a person confirms it.

items.description: The current result of one control for one subject. insufficient: the evidence does not settle it, or the control’s current version has not been evaluated yet. needs_confirmation: nothing checks it automatically; a person confirms it. not_applicable: the control is not in effect for the flight, or its applicability rule found it does not apply, with the recorded sentence as summary. A result is never a verdict and blocks nothing. evaluation.digest is canonicalDigest of the evaluation record.

subject.description: sourceId is present exactly when scope is source.

applicability.description: What route review recorded about whether this control applies to the flight: the outcome, its basis and what was measured. digest is canonicalDigest of the full applicability record, whose inputs are the list’s mission and this control version. The rule that decided it is the one the control’s pinned type declares, which the type’s digest commits, and what the control declares is in its parameters, so neither is repeated here.

notApplicable.description: The controls route review recorded as not applying, at most as many as one review considers; they are not repeated in controls.

items.description: One accepted control in force that route review recorded as not applying to the flight, with what was measured and the recorded sentence. It needs no briefing.

applicability.description: What route review recorded about whether this control applies to the flight: the outcome, its basis and what was measured. digest is canonicalDigest of the full applicability record, whose inputs are the list’s mission and this control version. The rule that decided it is the one the control’s pinned type declares, which the type’s digest commits, and what the control declares is in its parameters, so neither is repeated here.

mission.description: The exact mission revision route review read for this list, which every applicability record in it was evaluated against; null when no listed control needed route review.

standing.description: Whether the briefing counts at evaluatedAt, read from the database clock. It is in force before validUntil and lapsed from then on: its release window ends (release_window_end) or an accepted control that can matter to the flight starts or ends (control_boundary). A lapsed briefing cannot be acknowledged and does not count toward departure readiness; acknowledgements recorded before it lapsed stay recorded.
